US-119-HR10919.title: Safety Net Provider Drug Pricing Protection Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10919.description: To amend title III of the Public Health Service Act to ensure that certain safety net providers are not required to pay more than the 340B ceiling price for covered outpatient drugs at the time of purchase.
US-119-HR10919.aiSummary: The bill would require certain safety net health providers to pay no more than the 340B ceiling price for covered outpatient drugs when they buy them. It applies to certain covered entities and sole community hospitals. The change would take effect on the date it is enacted and would apply to drugs bought on or after that date.

US-119-HJRES220.title: Proposing an amendment to the Constitution of the United States relating to a national referendum process.

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on the Judiciary.
Introduced in House

US-119-HJRES220.aiSummary: The resolution would propose a Constitution change to create a national referendum process, where people could vote on laws or on repealing existing laws. To get on the ballot, a petition would need enough signatures from at least 25 states and from across the country, collected within 18 months. If a measure got 60% support, it would become law without going to the President, and Congress would face limits on changing it for 2 years unless two-thirds of each House agrees.

US-119-S2403.title: Retire through Ownership Act
US-119-S2403.summary:
Retire through Ownership Act

This act allows the fiduciary of an Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP) to rely on a valuation provided by an independent valuation expert or business appraiser in determining the fair market value of the plan's assets if the assets are not securities for which there is a generally recognized market and the expert or appraiser follows specified methodologies.

In general, ESOPs are defined contribution pension plans where employees accrue shares of their employers' stock in individual accounts as part of their compensation. After separating from employment or retiring, employees receive the cash value of their shares.

Under the act, an independent expert or appraiser must adhere to the methodology established under the Internal Revenue Service Ruling 59-60, which prescribes the factors a professional business appraiser should consider in forming a valuation of the stock for a closely held business.

US-119-S5659.title: Literacy Improvement for Transformation Act of 2026
committees: Senate Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions

actions.text: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.
Introduced in Senate

US-119-S5659.description: A bill to authorize the Secretary of Education to carry out a grant program to assist local educational agencies with ensuring that each elementary school and secondary school has at least one reading or literacy specialist on staff.
US-119-S5659.aiSummary: The bill would create a competitive Education Department grant program for local school agencies and some partners to help each elementary and secondary school have at least one full-time reading or literacy specialist. It would fund hiring, training, retention, and other support for these specialists, with a focus on schools serving students who struggle with reading. Grant recipients would have to report each year on their progress and how the money was used.

US-119-S5637.title: STRATA Act of 2026

actions.text: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Foreign Relations.
Introduced in Senate

US-119-S5637.description: A bill to establish the Critical Minerals Innovation Partnership, and for other purposes.
US-119-S5637.aiSummary: The bill would create a State Department program to help the United States work with chosen countries and groups on new critical minerals technology. Critical minerals are materials used in things like energy systems, semiconductors, and defense. It would set rules for who can join, block work with countries of concern and their entities, and require notice to Congress before new partnerships start.

committees: Senate Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions

Introduced in Senate

US-119-S5615.description: A bill to amend the Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938 to protect worker access to employer equity, and for other purposes.
US-119-S5615.aiSummary: This bill would change labor rules to say that certain employee stock awards called restricted stock units can be treated like other employer equity for overtime pay calculations. It would affect workers and employers that use these stock programs. The change would take effect 90 days after enactment, and some older stock grants would get limited protection from liability.

US-119-HR9809.title: Disabled Access Credit Modernization Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR9809.description: To amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to modify the disabled access credit, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR9809.aiSummary: The bill would change the disabled access tax credit for eligible small businesses. It would let the credit cover more kinds of costs, including changes to remove barriers, interpreters, readers, equipment changes, and similar help for people with disabilities. The new rules would apply to costs paid or incurred after December 31, 2026, and the Treasury Department would have to issue guidance and do outreach to small businesses.

US-119-S4845.title: Protect Our Polls Act

actions.text: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
Introduced in Senate

US-119-S4845.description: A bill to require explicit Congressional approval for troops or armed men at polling places for the only exception in the United States Code, and for other purposes.
US-119-S4845.aiSummary: The bill would require Congress to approve, before any deployment, the use of troops or armed men, including federal law enforcement officers, at polling places when they are sent to repel armed enemies of the United States. It would also set up a fast notice and review process for Congress and limit federal money for using troops or armed men to access certain election records. The changes to the Civil Rights Act of 1960 would end on January 20, 2029.

US-119-HR6938.title: Commerce, Justice, Science; Energy and Water Development; and Interior and Environment Appropriations Act, 2026
US-119-HR6938.summary:
Commerce, Justice, Science; Energy and Water Development; and Interior and Environment Appropriations Act, 2026

This bill provides FY2026 appropriations to several federal departments and agencies for activities and programs related to commerce, law enforcement, science, energy and water development, public lands, and the environment.

Specifically, the bill includes 3 of the 12 regular FY2026 appropriations bills:
• the Commerce, Justice, Science, and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 2026;
• the Energy and Water Development and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 2026; and
• the Department of the Interior, Environment, and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 2026.

The departments, agencies, and activities funded in the bill include
• the Department of Commerce,
• the Department of Justice,
• the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA),
• the National Science Foundation,
• U.S. Army Corps of Engineers civil works projects,
• the Department of Energy,
• the Department of the Interior,
• the Environmental Protection Agency,
• the Forest Service,
• the Indian Health Service, and
• several related and independent agencies.

The bill also sets forth requirements and restrictions for using funds provided by this and other appropriations acts.

US-119-HR1823.title: VA Budget Shortfall Accountability Act
US-119-HR1823.summary:
VA Budget Shortfall Accountability Act

This act requires the Government Accountability Office (GAO) to review and report on the circumstances and causes of the shortfall in funding of the Veterans Benefits Administration for FY2024 and the expected shortfall in funding of the Veterans Health Administration in FY2025. The Department of Veterans Affairs must submit such GAO report to Congress. For each of the five fiscal years following the date of enactment of this act, GAO must conduct subsequent reviews and reports regarding the funding of the VA.
